newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves German interest rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves German interest rates steady.

text.p: The German central bank left the key discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting Thursday.

The Bundesbank left the discount rate at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. It also left the bank's main money market rate, the repo, at a fixed 3 percent for the next two weeks.
Few economists had expected the central bank to take action on rates at the meeting, saying inflation was tame and the strengthening mark should not be provoked.
German financial markets showed little reaction to the decision.

All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters this week had said the central bank would keep rates on hold. Only one economist predicted a cut in the discount and Lombard rates this year while none predicted a rate rise during the rest of 1997.
Economists believe the German economy is showing signs of modest recovery and no danger of inflation, providing no reason for the Bundesbank to take action on rates in either direction.
